honesty.banner: Sample / demo dataset — not a live citizen-impact feed. These statements are illustrative educational patterns. They are not current-event reports or household advice.
honesty.confidenceRules: Observed is reserved for established facts. Downstream effects, why-analysis, and predicted household impacts must never use Observed. Missing or invalid confidence defaults to Unknown.
honesty.evidenceRules: Demo evidence uses example.invalid citations and historical pattern notes. Never treat these as live news.

linkage.relationshipExplorerStatus: Not on origin/main yet — soft-link deferred; entity IDs use stable gsn_* so Relationship Explorer can join later.

sections.label: Food
sections.blurb: Grocery availability, perishables, and household food-cost channels.

statements.whatChanged: In this sample scenario, a port authority reports slowed cargo handling during a labor stoppage. Time-sensitive food imports face longer dwell risk.
statements.why: Perishable foods and cold-chain windows are sensitive to terminal slowdowns. Households may notice thinner selection or higher prices if stoppages last — that pass-through is analysis, not an established fact.
statements.causedBy: Labor stoppage slows container terminals, delaying perishable imports into retail and food processing.

causeChain.label: Port labor stoppage
causeChain.explanation: Cargo handling slows or pauses during the stoppage.

causeChain.label: Imports / perishables
causeChain.explanation: Time-sensitive cargo faces dwell and spoilage risk.

causeChain.label: Retail / food
causeChain.explanation: Restock cadence and cold-chain windows tighten.

causeChain.label: Household food costs
causeChain.explanation: Spot gaps and price pressure are plausible if prolonged — not Observed.

sections.label: Fuel
sections.blurb: Pump availability, refined-fuel distribution, and commute-cost channels.

statements.whatChanged: In this sample scenario based on a well-known historical pattern, a pipeline operator reports a ransomware incident affecting business systems and temporarily pauses some operations.
statements.why: Even when malware hits IT systems, operators may pause physical product movement as a precaution. Local station shortages can appear within days if terminals starve — price paths remain uncertain and must not be labeled Observed.
statements.causedBy: Ransomware disrupts pipeline billing/operations systems, leading to a precautionary pause in refined-fuel movement.

causeChain.label: Ransomware on pipeline operator
causeChain.explanation: Operator reports ransomware affecting business systems.

causeChain.label: Fuel pipeline pause
causeChain.explanation: Precautionary pause can halt product movement.

causeChain.label: Gasoline / diesel
causeChain.explanation: Regional supply tightens if terminals starve.

causeChain.label: Fuel availability
causeChain.explanation: Local shortages possible; predicted price spikes are not Observed.

sections.label: Utilities
sections.blurb: Power, water, and heating/cooling reliability or cost notices.

statements.whatChanged: In this sample scenario, prolonged drought reduces water available for an illustrative canal and hydropower corridor. Operators publish capacity notices citing below-normal water levels.
statements.why: Lower reservoir or corridor water can constrain hydropower output and raise reliance on other generation. Household utility bills may shift over weeks to months depending on regional mix — that path is labeled analysis, not fact.
statements.causedBy: Prolonged drought reduces water available to shared corridor infrastructure that also supports generation.

causeChain.label: Prolonged drought
causeChain.explanation: Below-normal rainfall reduces water available to shared systems.

causeChain.label: Canal / hydropower corridor
causeChain.explanation: Water management notices reduce capacity on shared infrastructure.

causeChain.label: Regional power utility
causeChain.explanation: Generation mix may shift if hydropower is constrained.

causeChain.label: Household utility costs
causeChain.explanation: Bill effects depend on contracts and regional mix — not Observed.

sections.label: Housing
sections.blurb: Construction input costs and channels that can pressure rents or purchase budgets.

statements.whatChanged: In this sample scenario, a trade authority publishes higher tariff rates on selected steel product lines with an effective date.
statements.why: Steel is a common construction input. Higher landed costs can pressure project budgets over months. Pass-through to household housing costs is plausible but not automatic — contracts and inventories matter.
statements.causedBy: Illustrative steel tariffs raise import costs for fabricators and construction supply chains.

causeChain.label: Steel tariff
causeChain.explanation: Published tariff schedule takes effect on listed lines.

causeChain.label: Steel
causeChain.explanation: Landed cost of covered imports rises for importers.

causeChain.label: Construction
causeChain.explanation: Project budgets may absorb higher material costs.

causeChain.label: Housing costs
causeChain.explanation: Pass-through to housing materials is plausible, not certain.

sections.label: Travel
sections.blurb: Fares, delays, route friction, and fuel-sensitive travel costs.

statements.whatChanged: In this sample scenario, a maritime advisory notes carriers diverting sailings away from a contested corridor after security incidents, lengthening alternate routes.
statements.why: Longer voyages raise bunker fuel use and schedule uncertainty. Passenger and freight travel costs can become more sensitive over days to weeks — duration depends on security conditions that are not knowable from the advisory alone.
statements.causedBy: Corridor security risk prompts carriers to divert onto longer sea routes.

causeChain.label: Corridor diversion
causeChain.explanation: Carriers divert sailings after security advisories.

causeChain.label: Longer sea route
causeChain.explanation: Voyages add days via alternate Capes.

causeChain.label: Freight / fuel
causeChain.explanation: Bunker burn and schedule cost rise.

causeChain.label: Travel costs
causeChain.explanation: Fare and delay sensitivity are plausible — analysis only.

sections.label: Healthcare
sections.blurb: Access friction and supply channels for common medical goods — literacy, not clinical advice.

statements.whatChanged: In this sample scenario, the same coastal port stoppage that slows perishables also delays containerized medical-supply shipments reported in public port updates.
statements.why: Hospitals and clinics often hold buffers, but prolonged terminal delays can tighten restock windows for non-urgent supplies. Any household access effect is conditional and must stay Low/Medium — never Observed as a prediction.
statements.causedBy: Port labor stoppage delays containerized medical-supply shipments into healthcare logistics.

causeChain.label: Port labor stoppage
causeChain.explanation: Cargo handling slows during the stoppage.

causeChain.label: Medical supply shipments
causeChain.explanation: Containerized medical goods face longer dwell.

causeChain.label: Healthcare providers
causeChain.explanation: Restock buffers may tighten if delays persist.

causeChain.label: Access friction
causeChain.explanation: Household access effects are conditional — not clinical advice.

sections.label: Insurance
sections.blurb: Premium and coverage pressure channels after public cyber or infrastructure incidents.

statements.whatChanged: In this sample scenario, public reporting of a ransomware incident on critical energy infrastructure renews attention on cyber underwriting for similar operators.
statements.why: After visible cyber incidents, insurers may reprice cyber coverage for related sectors over months. Households usually feel this indirectly through business costs or specialized policies — treat as Low-confidence literacy, not a rate quote.
statements.causedBy: High-visibility ransomware on a fuel pipeline operator raises cyber underwriting attention for energy and adjacent sectors.

causeChain.label: Ransomware incident
causeChain.explanation: Public incident draws underwriting attention.

causeChain.label: Cyber insurance
causeChain.explanation: Underwriters may adjust terms for similar operators.

causeChain.label: Premium / coverage pressure
causeChain.explanation: Indirect household effects are possible — not Observed rate changes.

sections.label: Technology
sections.blurb: Device and component availability when chip supply chains tighten.

statements.whatChanged: In this sample educational scenario, illustrative export-control language and concentrated advanced-chip production highlight how device makers depend on a narrow set of inputs.
statements.why: When advanced chips are scarce or delayed, electronics and device makers may stretch lead times. Households might notice longer waits or higher prices for some devices over months — concentration literacy, not a geopolitical verdict.
statements.causedBy: Illustrative export-control policy plus concentrated advanced-chip capacity can constrain device manufacturing inputs.

causeChain.label: Export-control policy
causeChain.explanation: Illustrative controls can limit certain advanced-chip flows.

causeChain.label: Advanced chips
causeChain.explanation: Constrained inputs raise allocation pressure.

causeChain.label: Device manufacturing
causeChain.explanation: Lead times stretch when chip supply tightens.

causeChain.label: Device availability
causeChain.explanation: Households may notice delays — literacy only, not a forecast.
